entries.mechanism: Axiom encodes 2.05 (200% + the 5-point MAGI disregard) from the CMS Medicaid/CHIP eligibility-levels table, which predates Alaska's expansion. Alaska added an optional eligibility group for pregnant women with income 201%-225% FPL and 12-month postpartum coverage via a Medicaid state plan amendment effective February 2024, making the effective limit 230% (225% + 5). PolicyEngine's 2.30 matches the current authoritative level (KFF, as of January 2026: Alaska pregnant women 230%). Axiom's cited CMS table snapshot is stale; the encoding needs the 2024 expansion.

Axiom encodes 3.80 (375% + the 5-point MAGI disregard) from the CMS eligibility-levels table, which predates Iowa's reduction. Iowa SF 2251 (2024) directed HHS to lower the Medicaid income limit for infants and pregnant women to 215% FPL (220% effective with the disregard); CMS approved the SPA in January 2025 and the reduction took effect during 2025, so Axiom's 3.80 no longer reflects Iowa law for 2026. PolicyEngine's 3.05 matches KFF's January-2026 infant figure for Iowa (305%), which reflects the highest Medicaid/CHIP- funded infant coverage (hawk-i CHIP), not the Medicaid-only limit either; neither engine currently carries the Medicaid-only 2.20. Classified as an Axiom encoding gap because Axiom's cited CMS snapshot is stale against the authoritative 2025 change.

Axiom encodes 1.75 (170% + the 5-point MAGI disregard), the pre-2024 North Dakota children's level. CMS-approved SPAs ND-24-0007 and companion ND-24-0101 raised the income standard for children (including the title XXI-funded Medicaid expansion) from 170% to 200% FPL effective 2024-01-01, an effective 205% with the disregard. PolicyEngine's 2.05 matches the authoritative post-SPA level; Axiom's cited CMS table snapshot is stale.

Axiom encodes 1.65 (160% + the 5-point MAGI disregard), Nevada's pre-2024 pregnant-women level. CMS-approved SPA NV-23-0030 raised pregnant-women eligibility to 185% FPL (190% effective) from January 2024, and Nevada subsequently raised it again (SPA 25-0006 to 190% effective July 2025, then to a 200% income standard per Nevada Medicaid web announcement 3748 of 2025-10-20; KFF reports 205% effective as of January 2026). PolicyEngine's 1.90 matches the 2024 level and is itself one update behind, but Axiom's 1.65 is stale against every post-2023 authoritative level, so the row is an Axiom encoding gap first. The pinned difference matches the 2024 SPA step.

Scope difference between two current, defensible readings. Axiom's concept is the Medicaid-only effective limit for pregnant women: 1.95 (190% Medicaid + the 5-point MAGI disregard), matching the CMS eligibility-levels table (RI pregnant Medicaid 190%). PolicyEngine's pregnant income_limit parameter stores the highest pregnancy coverage including Rhode Island's CHIP-funded coverage: 2.58 (253% CHIP + 5), matching both the CMS table's Pregnant Women CHIP column (253%) and KFF's January-2026 RI CHIP figure (258%). The residual is exactly the Medicaid-vs-CHIP column gap; neither engine misstates its source.

Axiom's 2.00 is the CMS eligibility-levels table value for TennCare infants (195% Medicaid + the 5-point MAGI disregard), corroborated by KFF's January-2026 infant table (Tennessee 195%). PolicyEngine stores a flat 2.16 for all Tennessee child age bands, unchanged since its 2018-01-01 entry, which matches neither the Medicaid infant level (195%/200% effective) nor CoverKids separate CHIP (250%/255% effective) in any current source. No PolicyEngine issue tracks the Tennessee children's limits.

Scope difference between two current, defensible readings. Axiom's concept is the Medicaid-only effective limit: 2.00 (TennCare for Pregnant Women at 195% + the 5-point MAGI disregard), matching the CMS eligibility-levels table (Tennessee pregnant Medicaid 195%, Pregnant CHIP N/A because CoverKids maternity coverage runs through the unborn-child option). PolicyEngine's 2.55 is the highest pregnancy coverage including CoverKids CHIP-funded maternity coverage at 250% FPL (+5), the figure KFF reports for Tennessee as of January 2026 (255%). The residual is exactly the Medicaid-vs-CoverKids gap; neither engine misstates its source.

Axiom encodes 1.98 (193% + the 5-point MAGI disregard) from the CMS eligibility-levels table, which predates Washington's expansion. The Washington Health Care Authority raised the income limit for Apple Health for pregnant individuals (and After-Pregnancy Coverage) to 210% FPL effective 2024-11-01, an effective 215% with the disregard. PolicyEngine's 2.15 matches the current authoritative level (WA HCA; KFF as of January 2026: Washington 215%). Axiom's cited CMS table snapshot is stale.
